FDG-PET/CT cartography showed an 82.1% reduction in tracheobronchial cartilage SUVmax in the active arm. Conclusions: Dual TL1A and IL-23p19 blockade enables glucocorticoid withdrawal and suppresses airway chondritis in relapsing polychondritis.

Background: Schistosoma mansoni periportal pipe-stem fibrosis persists after praziquantel eradication in hyperendemic regions and leads to non-cirrhotic portal hypertension and variceal hemorrhage. Methods: In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial (SCHISTO-LOXL2) in Kisumu and Mwanza, 188 praziquantel-cured adults with ultrasound-Confirmed Niamey pattern D or E periportal fibrosis and spleen stiffness >45 kPa received an oral selective lysyl oxidase-like 2 and IL-13R-alpha-2 modulator, PXS-6302 (100 mg once daily, n=94), or placebo (n=94) for 36 weeks. Results: Portal vein wall thickness and periportal collagen band diameter regressed by 34.8% in PXS-6302 recipients versus 4.2% in placebo controls (p<0.0001), while transient elastography spleen stiffness decreased by -14.6 kPa versus -1.8 kPa (p<0.0001). Esophageal variceal grade improved by >=1 grade on endoscopy in 48.9% of treated patients versus 12.8% of controls. Conclusions: Oral LOXL2/IL-13 pathway inhibition reverses established periportal fibrosis and portal hypertension after schistosomiasis cure.

Background: Severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (PiZZ genotype) causes toxic polymerization of Z-AAT within hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum and panacinar emphysema due to uninhibited neutrophil elastase. Methods: In the phase 2a ALPHA-EDIT9 trial across nine European and US centers, 48 adults with PiZZ alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and both liver fibrosis (F2-F3) and emphysema received a single intravenous infusion of lipid-nanoparticle-formulated adenine base editor mRNA and guide RNA correcting the SERPINA1 c.1024G>A (Glu342Lys) mutation (ABE-SERP1, 0.6 mg/kg). Results: At week 24, total serum AAT rose from a median of 4.6 umol/L to 23.8 umol/L (IQR, 19.4 to 28.1; normal range >20 umol/L), with wild-type M-AAT accounting for 91.4% of circulating protein by mass spectrometry. Paired liver biopsies at week 48 showed an 84.2% clearance of diastase-resistant PAS-positive Z-polymer globules. Conclusions: Single-dose in vivo adenine base editing restores physiological wild-type M-AAT levels and clears hepatic Z-polymers in PiZZ deficiency.

Background: Sjogren disease is characterized by salivary and lacrimal gland ectopic germinal center formation driven by CXCL13, CD40-CD40L interactions, and type I interferon signatures. Methods: In the 48-week phase 2b SJOGREN-CD40L trial across 21 rheumatology centers, 192 patients with active primary Sjogren disease (ESSDAI >=6 and stimulated salivary flow >=0.1 mL/min) were randomized 1:1:1 to a platelet-sparing Fc-silent anti-CD40L Fab-albumin fusion protein, DAZ-302 (300 mg SC every 4 weeks, n=64; 150 mg SC every 4 weeks, n=64), or placebo (n=64). Results: At week 48, mean ESSDAI decreased by -6.8 points in the 300-mg arm and -5.4 points in the 150-mg arm compared with -2.1 points in the placebo arm (both p<0.0001). EULAR Sjogren Syndrome Patient Reported Index dryness and fatigue scores improved by -2.9 points with 300-mg DAZ-302 versus -0.7 points with placebo (p<0.0001), with zero thromboembolic events. Conclusions: Fc-silent CD40L blockade reduces systemic activity and glandular symptoms in primary Sjogren disease.

Background: Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (Kennedy disease) is an X-linked adult-onset motor neuronopathy and myopathy caused by CAG trinucleotide expansion in the androgen receptor gene. Methods: In the 52-week randomized double-blind KENNEDY-PROTAC7 trial across eight Japanese and Italian neurological institutes, 114 men with genetically confirmed spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (CAG repeat length 42-54) received an orally bioavailable skeletal-muscle- and motor-neuron-penetrant androgen receptor N-terminal domain PROTAC degrader, ARD-258 (60 mg once daily, n=76), or placebo (n=38). Results: Quadriceps biopsy at week 16 demonstrated an 88.3% degradation of nuclear polyQ-expanded androgen receptor aggregates without suppressing serum luteinizing hormone or endogenous testosterone. At week 52, the Adult Myopathy Assessment Tool total score improved by +4.6 points in ARD-258 recipients versus -2.8 points in placebo controls (p<0.0001), and serum creatine kinase declined by 61.4%. Conclusions: Targeted degradation of polyglutamine-expanded androgen receptor improves motor function in Kennedy disease.

Background: Systemic mastocytosis with an associated hematologic neoplasm (SM-AHN) frequently harbors KIT D816V alongside SRSF2, ASXL1, or RUNX1 mutations that confer resistance to avapritinib or midostaurin. Methods: In the multicenter phase 2 MAST-DUAL12 study, 86 patients with KIT D816V-positive SM-AHN and at least one high-risk myeloid spliceosome or epigenetic co-mutation received the brain-sparing selective KIT D816V inhibitor bezuclastinib (150 mg daily) combined with oral decitabine/cedazuridine (35/100 mg days 1-5 of each 28-day cycle). Results: Modified IWG-MRT-ECNM overall response rate was 77.9% (67/86), including 41.9% complete remission with full or partial hematologic recovery. Bone marrow mast cell burden declined by >=90% in 84.9% of patients, KIT D816V digital droplet PCR variant allele fraction fell below 0.1% in 53.5%, and 24-month overall survival was 74.4%. Conclusions: Combined selective KIT D816V inhibition and oral hypomethylating therapy achieves deep molecular responses in high-risk SM-AHN.

Background: Tardive dyskinesia results from chronic dopamine D2 receptor blockade-induced supersensitivity and striatal cholinergic interneuron dysfunction, while VMAT2 inhibitors can cause parkinsonism, depression, and akathisia. Methods: In the 12-week randomized double-blind TARDIVE-M4 trial across 16 psychiatric centers, 168 adults with moderate-to-severe tardive dyskinesia (Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale dyskinesia score >=10) on stable antipsychotic therapy were randomized 1:1 to a selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator, CVL-865 (25 mg once daily, n=84), or placebo (n=84). Results: Mean AIMS total dyskinesia score (items 1-7) decreased by -5.6 points in the CVL-865 group compared with -1.4 points in the placebo group (least-squares mean difference, -4.2; p<0.0001). A >=50% AIMS reduction occurred in 60.7% versus 15.5% of patients (p<0.0001), with no worsening of Simpson-Angus parkinsonism or Montgomery-Asberg depression ratings. Conclusions: Selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulation reduces tardive dyskinesia without monoamine depletion side effects.

Background: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is caused by autoantibody-mediated severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, and standard caplacizumab plus plasma exchange still requires prolonged immunosuppression and plasma exposure. Methods: In the multicenter randomized phase 3 TTP-GAIN14 trial across 17 hematology centers, 116 patients presenting with acute immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (ADAMTS13 activity <2%) were randomized 1:1 to receive a glycan-shielded autoantibody-resistant gain-of-function recombinant ADAMTS13 variant, rADAMTS13-R568K (80 IU/kg daily IV until platelet normalization, then weekly for 4 weeks, plus rituximab, without plasma exchange, n=58) or standard daily plasma exchange plus caplacizumab and rituximab (n=58). Results: Median time to platelet count normalization (>=150x10^9/L) was 2.4 days (IQR, 1.8 to 3.2) in the plasma-free rADAMTS13-R568K arm versus 3.9 days (IQR, 2.9 to 5.4) in the plasma exchange arm (p<0.0001). Clinical exacerbation or relapse within 60 days occurred in 1.7% versus 12.1% (p=0.028). Conclusions: Autoantibody-resistant recombinant ADAMTS13 enables rapid plasma-exchange-free remission in acute immune TTP.

Background: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy progresses despite tetramer stabilization or hepatic TTR silencing because preexisting myocardial amyloid fibrils remain cleared slowly by endogenous macrophages. Methods: In the 18-month randomized double-blind AMYLOID-CLEAR9 phase 2b trial across 20 cardiology centers, 180 patients with wild-type or variant ATTR cardiomyopathy (NYHA class II-III) on stable tafamidis background received a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting a cryptic conformational epitope on misfolded monomeric/fibrillar TTR, NI-308 (30 mg/kg intravenously every 4 weeks, n=120), or placebo (n=60). Results: Cardiac 124I-evuzamitide PET/CT and cardiac MRI extracellular volume mapping at month 12 demonstrated a mean myocardial extracellular volume reduction of -11.4% (from 52.8% to 41.4%) in NI-308 recipients versus +2.6% in placebo controls (p<0.0001). NT-proBNP decreased by 48.2% versus +11.9% (p<0.0001), and left ventricular global longitudinal strain improved by -2.9% (p=0.0002). Conclusions: Conformational anti-TTR antibody therapy actively depletes established cardiac amyloid deposits on top of tafamidis.

Background: Tuberous sclerosis complex-associated lymphangioleiomyomatosis causes progressive cystic lung destruction in women, and mTORC1 inhibition with sirolimus is purely cytostatic, with lung function decline resuming upon discontinuation. Methods: In the phase 2 LAM-AUTOPH8 trial across nine rare lung disease centers, 84 women with TSC- or sporadic-LAM and FEV1 <80% predicted on stable sirolimus were randomized 1:1 to add an inhaled selective ULK1/2 autophagy kinase inhibitor and GPX4 ferroptosis sensitizer, LAM-404 (20 mg once daily via dry-powder inhaler, n=42), or placebo (n=42) for 24 weeks, followed by a 16-week sirolimus withdrawal phase. Results: Serum VEGF-D declined by 69.4% in the LAM-404 plus sirolimus group versus 8.2% in sirolimus plus placebo controls (p<0.0001). During the 16-week treatment-free withdrawal phase, mean FEV1 remained stable (-14 mL) in prior LAM-404 recipients versus a rapid decline (-186 mL) in controls (p<0.0001). Conclusions: Inhaled ULK1/2 and GPX4 dual targeting converts cytostatic mTOR blockade into cytotoxic clearance of LAM cells.

Background: Ulcerative pyoderma gangrenosum is a neutrophilic dermatosis characterized by painful, rapidly expanding necrotic skin ulcers with high morbidity from prolonged high-dose systemic corticosteroids. Methods: In the multicenter randomized double-blind PYODERMA-C5A11 trial across 14 dermatology departments, 96 patients with active ulcerative pyoderma gangrenosum (target ulcer area 5 to 60 cm2) were randomized 2:1 to an oral selective C5aR1 and CXCR1/2 dual antagonist, DFX-702 (40 mg twice daily, n=64), or oral prednisolone (0.75 mg/kg/day tapered over 16 weeks, n=32) without concomitant systemic steroids in the DFX-702 arm. Results: Complete target ulcer healing at week 16 was achieved in 62.5% of DFX-702 recipients (40/64) compared with 37.5% of prednisolone recipients (12/32; p=0.020). Median time to arrest of ulcer edge cribriform progression and >=50% pain reduction was 6 days with DFX-702 versus 15 days with prednisolone (p<0.0001), with fewer serious infections (1.6% vs 18.8%). Conclusions: Steroid-free oral C5aR1/CXCR1/2 blockade accelerates ulcer healing and pain resolution in pyoderma gangrenosum.

Background: Urea cycle disorders such as ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency cause life-threatening hyperammonemic crises and cognitive disability despite dietary protein restriction and nitrogen-scavenging drugs. Methods: In the phase 2 UREA-MRNA16 crossover study across seven metabolic genetics centers, 36 adolescents and adults with late-onset ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency received biweekly intravenous infusions of hepatocyte-targeted GalNAc-lipid nanoparticles encapsulating codon-optimized human OTC mRNA with stabilized 3-prime UTRs (LNP-hOTC, 0.35 mg/kg every 14 days) or placebo for 12 weeks per period. Results: Quantitative 13C-acetate breath/plasma ureagenesis rate increased by 3.8-fold during LNP-hOTC treatment compared with placebo (reaching 78.4% of healthy control ureagenesis; p<0.0001). Peak 24-hour plasma ammonia fell from a mean of 94.2 to 28.6 umol/L (p<0.0001), allowing all 36 participants to discontinue sodium phenylbutyrate while doubling dietary natural protein intake without hyperammonemic episodes. Conclusions: Biweekly GalNAc-LNP OTC mRNA replacement restores hepatic ureagenesis and eliminates scavenger dependency in OTC deficiency.

Background: Visceral leishmaniasis in East Africa caused by Leishmania donovani shows suboptimal cure rates and high toxicity with sodium stibogluconate plus paromomycin or liposomal amphotericin B. Methods: In a randomized, open-label, non-inferiority and superiority phase 3 trial (LEISH-CLK12) in Gondar, Gedaref, and Pokot, 340 immunocompetent patients aged 6 to 55 years with parasitologically confirmed visceral leishmaniasis were randomized 1:1 to a 10-day oral regimen of the parasite CDC2-related kinase 12 (CRK12) inhibitor LXE-408 (100 mg twice daily) plus miltefosine (n=170) or 17-day intramuscular sodium stibogluconate plus paromomycin (n=170). Results: Definitive cure at 6 months (absence of clinical relapse and negative splenic or bone marrow aspirate) was 96.5% (164/170) in the oral LXE-408/miltefosine arm versus 87.6% (149/170) in the injectable standard-care arm (difference, +8.8%; 95% CI, 3.1 to 14.6; p=0.0024 for superiority). Grade >=3 hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, or cardiotoxicity occurred in 1.8% versus 14.1% (p<0.0001). Conclusions: A 10-day all-oral CRK12 inhibitor regimen achieves superior cure and safety in East African visceral leishmaniasis.

Background: Warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia mediated by pan-reactive IgG autoantibodies against erythrocyte Rh or glycophorin antigens often relapses after corticosteroids and rituximab. Methods: In the 24-week randomized double-blind WAIHA-SYK9 trial across 15 hematology centers, 110 adults with relapsing or refractory warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia and hemoglobin <9.5 g/dL received an oral reversible covalent Bruton tyrosine kinase and spleen tyrosine kinase dual inhibitor, PRN-518 (80 mg once daily, n=74), or placebo (n=36). Results: Durable hemoglobin response (>=10.0 g/dL with a >=2.0 g/dL increase from baseline over >=4 consecutive weeks without transfusion) was achieved by 68.9% of PRN-518 recipients (51/74) versus 11.1% of placebo controls (4/36; p<0.0001). Median time to response was 13 days, lactate dehydrogenase and unconjugated bilirubin normalized in 74.3% of responders, and direct antiglobulin test IgG titer declined by >=4 dilutions in 58.1%. Conclusions: Dual BTK/SYK inhibition rapidly halts splenic erythrophagocytosis and autoantibody production in warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

Background: Wilson disease causes hepatic and lenticular copper toxicosis due to ATP7B deficiency, and oral chelators such as D-penicillamine or trientine trigger paradoxical neurological worsening in up to 25% of patients by mobilizing free non-ceruloplasmin copper into the central nervous system. Methods: In the randomized double-blind WILSON-METH10 phase 3 trial across 13 European and Asian movement disorder and hepatology centers, 128 newly diagnosed or chelator-intolerant Wilson disease patients with predominant neurologic manifestations (Unified Wilson Disease Rating Scale neurological subscore >=15) were randomized 1:1 to a blood-brain-barrier-impermeable bis-choline tetrathiomolybdate and intestinal CTR1 copper-importer blocker combination, WTX-204 (30 mg daily, n=64), or trientine dihydrochloride (n=64) for 48 weeks. Results: Early paradoxical neurological deterioration (>4-point UWDRS increase within 12 weeks) occurred in 1.6% of WTX-204 recipients versus 21.9% of trientine recipients (p=0.0003). At week 48, mean UWDRS neurological score improved by -11.8 points with WTX-204 versus -3.9 points with trientine (p<0.0001). Conclusions: Dual CTR1 blockade and albumin-bound copper complexation improves neurologic recovery without early paradoxical deterioration in Wilson disease.

Background: X-linked hypophosphatemia caused by PHEX loss-of-function variants elevates fibroblast growth factor 23, leading to renal phosphate wasting, osteomalacia, and disabling enthesopathy that remains unresponsive to anti-FGF23 antibody therapy in adults. Methods: In the 52-week randomized double-blind XLH-ENPP20 trial across 10 adult metabolic bone clinics, 102 adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia and progressive spinal or Achilles calcific enthesopathy on burosumab were randomized 1:1 to add an oral selective FGFR1c/Klotho allosteric modulator and tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase attenuator, XLH-815 (50 mg once daily, n=51), or placebo (n=51). Results: Whole-spine low-dose CT syndesmophyte and enthesophyte calcification volume decreased by -14.2% in the XLH-815 group versus an increase of +18.7% in placebo controls (p<0.0001). Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index stiffness and physical function scores improved by 24.6 points versus 3.1 points (p<0.0001), while serum phosphate remained within 2.9 to 3.8 mg/dL. Conclusions: Allosteric FGFR1c/TNALP modulation arrests and regresses calcific enthesopathy in adult X-linked hypophosphatemia.
